status: exploratory: not pre-registered, one repetition, not evidence for a research question (R6.2, R6.3)
question: which verification conditions, taken whole before any tactic splits them, are hard for every prover alone; and on which does the outcome of a prover depend on its random seed (a baseline of hard, valid goals for lemma sharing)
repository_commit: df2d2a7 (dp-frontend, release build); eval/scripts/unsplit_baseline.py is new and uncommitted at the time of the run

corpora.creusat: https://github.com/sarsko/CreuSAT at 232edff08ec6a5713cc3d61797f353550ca94d6f, the 143 Coma files of verif/ as the project commits them, with the provers of the project's why3find.json
corpora.creusot-examples: the 63 Coma files under examples/ of the pinned Creusot (v0.15.0, fd4d85b2), its subdirectories included (matrix-2026-11-18 took 27 files), with the provers of Creusot's why3find.json

tools.proving: the pinned tools of this repository's development shell: Creusot 0.15.0 (prelude and prover configuration), Why3 1.8.2+git, why3find 1.3.0+dev with patches/why3find, dp-frontend

method: unsplit_baseline.py measure --seconds 5: every Coma file proved by dp-frontend with the project's why3find.json changed to depth 0 and no tactics, through corpus_hardness.py with DP_MATRIX_SECONDS=5: every prover alone on every verification condition at a reference limit of 5 s. The two corpora ran side by side
unsplit_baseline.py measure --seconds 60 --unproved-at 5: the same at 60 s on the 48 files with a verification condition that no prover proved at 5 s

unsplit_baseline.py seeds --seconds 5 --seeds 1,2,3,4,5: Z3, cvc5 and CVC4 run directly on the Printed_Goals that dp-frontend exported, once per seed, six runs at a time. dp-frontend exports the print of a prover only where why3find itself called that prover, so the runs cover Z3 on 326 verification conditions, cvc5 on 152 and CVC4 on 142: those that the provers before them in why3find's order did not prove at once, and all 87 that are not easy. Alt-Ergo has no seed option
unsplit_baseline.py seeds --seconds 60 --seeds 1,2,3 --at 5: the same at 60 s on the 87 verification conditions that are not easy, eight runs at a time

unsplit_baseline.py summarize: classes easy (some prover alone within 5 s), hard (none within 5 s, one within 60 s), out-of-reach (none within 60 s); a verification condition is unstable when a prover proves it with some seeds and not with others at one limit

files.creusat-5s/, creusat-60s/, creusot-examp: output of corpus_hardness.py: records/ (one line per prover run, as in matrix-2026-11-18), goals.jsonl, runs.jsonl
files.vcs.jsonl: every verification condition with its class, the run of every prover, and its seed runs
files.hard.jsonl: the 87 that are hard or out of reach, with the Task_Hash per prover and the provers that prove them at 60 s
files.unstable.jsonl: the 22 on which a prover's outcome depends on its seed
files.goals.tar.gz: the Printed_Goals of the 87 hard and out-of-reach verification conditions, one file per prover, named by Task_Hash (348 files, 101 MB unpacked)

findings.classes: 4070 verification conditions (601 of CreuSAT, 3469 of the examples): 3983 easy, 17 hard, 70 out of reach. CreuSAT has 2 hard and 5 out of reach, the examples 15 and 65
findings.validity: the 87 are taken to be valid because their projects keep every file proved with tactics: matrix-2026-11-18 proved all files of CreuSAT and the 27 example files of that run; the other 36 example files were not proved with tactics here
findings.where: CreuSAT: one in each of seven functions. Examples: red_black_tree 9, bounded_mpmc_queue 12 in two files, iterators/19_chain 6, doubly_linked_list 5, iterators/06_map_precond 5, and 35 more files with one to three
findings.hard: of the 17 hard ones, 9 are proved at 60 s by cvc5, 10 by Alt-Ergo and 3 by Z3 (some by two); none by CVC4. Their fastest proofs take between 7.5 s and 48 s
findings.one_prover: 51 easy verification conditions are proved within 5 s by exactly one of the four provers
findings.seeds: 22 verification conditions are unstable: 15 easy, 4 hard, 3 out of reach; the unstable prover is Z3 on 15 of them (21 of the 29 unstable prover-limit pairs). 8 that are not easy are proved within 5 s by some seed of some prover. At 60 s, 10 of the 17 hard ones are proved by every seed of some seeded prover, 3 by some seeds only, and 4 by no seed (Alt-Ergo alone proves those); of the 70 out of reach, 66 are proved by no seed of any prover, 3 by some seeds, and 1 by every seed of a prover that the first pass counted as failing
findings.reading: the stable pool for lemma sharing is small and concrete: 17 goals that one prover proves whole in 7 to 48 s and the others do not, and 66 valid goals that no prover and no seed proves whole within 60 s although their split pieces are easy. Seeds change little: a race of seeds would turn about 8 of the 87 into easy goals

caveats: one repetition; the machine was busy with other work (load average 8 to 16 on 14 cores during the passes), so outcomes near a limit may differ on a quiet machine

the limits of the first two passes are reference limits, which dp-frontend scales by each prover's Calibration; the seed runs use the limit in seconds as it is, and judge a run by the solver's first line of output and not by Why3's driver. On the pairs that both measured, the seed runs agree with the first pass in all but 4 of 620 cases beyond those counted as unstable
the seed runs do not cover the easy verification conditions that an earlier prover of why3find's order proves at once, so the count of unstable easy ones is a lower bound
seeds 1 to 5 (1 to 3 at 60 s) are few: a goal that no seed proved may be proved by a sixth
the examples corpus is 63 files here and was 27 in matrix-2026-11-18, so the counts of the two runs are not of the same goals
